editorial.headline: Stationery Retail Is Nationally Open, but Closed to PMA Registration in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity spans everyday writing and drawing supplies, open nationally to full foreign ownership but blocked for PMA registration across Bali.
editorial.body:
Retail trade in writing and drawing supplies is broader than the quiet image of a neighbourhood stationery counter might suggest. It covers the retail sale of pencils, pens, markers, ballpoint pens, sign pens and mechanical pencils, alongside compasses, drawing brushes, technical pens, crayons and pastels. The scope also reaches into whiteboards, drawing tables, screen-printing equipment, typewriter ribbons, watercolours and oil paints, as well as erasers, correction fluid or tape, ink, sharpeners, rulers and chalk. It is, in other words, the retail activity for a business trading in the practical tools of writing, marking, drawing and presentation.

The classification is open across every stated business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That matters because the activity is not confined in the record to one size of operator or one narrow retail format. A business may register this activity whether its commercial footing is micro, small, medium or large, provided its retail trade sits within the stated range of writing and drawing supplies. The scope is specific in its merchandise, but not slight: it includes both the everyday implements of school and office use and the materials and equipment associated with drawing, painting and screen printing.

At the national level, the position is unequivocal. The PMA status is TERBUKA, with a national foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. The cited basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For an investor considering the activity on a national basis, that is the relevant opening: the code is open to PMA and permits foreign ownership up to the stated ceiling.

Bali is the decisive exception. A foreigner cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today. At the Besar scale, OSS risk is recorded as Rendah or Menengah-Rendah across every scope, and Bali's permanent, island-wide moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA. The Bali status is therefore Blocked (risk class). This is not a qualification of the national ownership ceiling; it is a separate Bali registration barrier. The activity remains nationally open, but that openness does not create a PMA registration route in Bali while the stated moratorium applies.
editorial.pullQuote: The activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership, but Bali offers no PMA registration route for it today.
